items.q: Synthetic: angiography of a 34 year old woman shows a beaded mid renal artery. The likely cause is

x.key: **Fibromuscular dysplasia** gives the beaded look: short rings of narrowing alternate with small bulges in the middle of the artery.
x.notes:
## What it is
- A non-inflammatory, non-atherosclerotic disease of the **medium-sized arteries**
- Mostly **young and middle-aged women**
- Renal and internal carotid arteries are the usual sites

## Telling it apart
| Feature | Fibromuscular dysplasia | Atheroma | Arteritis of the aorta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Age | Young women | Older adults | Young women |
| Site | Middle and far artery | Origin of the artery | Aorta and its branches |
| Look | String of beads | Single tight narrowing | Long smooth narrowing |

## Next steps
1. Suspect it in young-onset high blood pressure
2. Confirm on angiography
3. Treat with balloon angioplasty

others.A: Atheroma narrows the **origin** of the artery in older people, not the middle.
others.B: Arteritis gives long, smooth narrowing of the aorta and its branches.
others.D: Hereditary telangiectasia makes small vascular malformations, not beading.

x.pearl: Mid-artery beads in a young woman: fibromuscular dysplasia. Origin narrowing in an older smoker: atheroma.
